messages.content: What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?

message.content:
The lion (*Panthera leo*) and the zebra (*Equus quagga*) belong to very different branches of the mammalian tree: lions are felids (order Carnivora) while zebras are equids (order Perissodactyla).  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the two orders, which is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria).  

That ancestor lived roughly 100 – 110 million years ago, during the early Cretaceous, before the diversification of the major placental lineages that eventually gave rise to carnivores, odd‑toed ungulates, primates, rodents, etc. In other words, the lion and zebra share a very ancient common ancestor that is shared by all placental mammals.
